question: Which of the following describes the 'Mutual Exclusion' condition required for a deadlock?
options: Resources can only be shared in a mutually exclusive manner so only one process holds a single-instance resource
Processes are allowed to preempt resources from lower-priority jobs at any time
All processes release all resources simultaneously before requesting new ones
Resources are infinitely available to any requesting process without queueing
evidence_quote: A resource can only be shared in mutually exclusive manner. It implies, if two process cannot use the same resource at the same time.
explanation: Mutual exclusion specifies that at least one resource must be held in a non-shareable mode by one process at a time.

question: How does the 'Hold and Wait' condition contribute to system deadlocks?
options: A process is completely blocked from holding any resources while running
A process currently holding allocated resources simultaneously waits to acquire additional resources held by other processes
Processes immediately release all resources if a requested resource is unavailable
The operating system terminates any process that holds more than one resource
evidence_quote: Hold and Wait: A process waits for some resources while holding another resource at the same time.
explanation: Hold and wait occurs when a thread or process retains already allocated resources while awaiting newly requested ones.

question: What is the defining attribute of the 'No Preemption' condition in deadlock theory?
options: Resources are preempted automatically whenever a higher priority process arrives
Resources can only be released voluntarily by the process holding them after task completion
The CPU scheduler forcibly swaps resource handles between concurrent processes
All allocated memory is reclaimed by the kernel every fixed time slice
evidence_quote: No preemption: The process which once scheduled will be executed till the completion. Resources will only be released when Process voluntarily relinquishes it.
explanation: Under no preemption, resources cannot be forcibly confiscated from a process; only the holding process can release them.

question: Why is the Circular Wait condition a necessary condition for deadlock?
options: It guarantees that all threads execute in strictly linear alphabetical order
It creates a closed chain of processes where each process waits for a resource held by the next process in the cycle
It forces all resources to be single-instance tape drives
It eliminates the need for mutual exclusion among threads
evidence_quote: Circular Wait: All the processes must be waiting for the resources in a cyclic manner so that the last process is waiting for the resource held by the first process.
explanation: Circular wait closes the dependency loop: P0 waits for P1, P1 waits for P2, ..., Pn waits for P0, leaving no unblocked process to break the cycle.

question: In the Banker's Algorithm, what formula determines the Need matrix for process Pi?
options: Need[i, j] = Max[i, j] + Allocation[i, j]
Need[i, j] = Max[i, j] - Allocation[i, j]
Need[i, j] = Available[j] - Allocation[i, j]
Need[i, j] = Allocation[i, j] / Max[i, j]
evidence_quote: Need [ i, j ] = Max [ i, j ] – Allocation [ i, j ]
explanation: The remaining resource need equals the declared maximum minus the instances currently allocated to that process.

question: What distinguishes deadlock avoidance from deadlock prevention?
options: Avoidance requires dynamic runtime inspection of system safe states using known future resource limits, whereas prevention restricts one of the four necessary conditions statically
Avoidance lets deadlocks happen and then reboots the machine, whereas prevention prevents system rebooting
Avoidance only works for single-instance resources, while prevention only works for multi-instance resources
There is no theoretical or practical difference between the two terms
evidence_quote: Prevention is done by negating one of necessary conditions. Avoidance checks continuously whether granting a request preserves a safe state.
explanation: Deadlock avoidance dynamically validates that the system remains in a safe state before granting requests, while prevention structurally disallows one of the 4 conditions.

question: What is the cardinality of the power set P(S) of a finite set S with n elements?
options: 2n
n!
evidence_quote: A power set of a set S is defined by P(S) = {A : A ⊆ S}. The number of elements is 2^n.
explanation: Every element of S has two choices (included or excluded) in any subset, yielding 2^n total subsets.

question: A binary relation R on set A is defined as symmetric if which of the following holds?
options: (a, a) ∈ R for all a ∈ A
Whenever (a, b) ∈ R, then (b, a) ∈ R for all a, b ∈ A
Whenever (a, b) ∈ R and (b, c) ∈ R, then (a, c) ∈ R
If (a, b) ∈ R and (b, a) ∈ R, then a must equal b
evidence_quote: A relation R on a set A is called symmetric if (b, a) ∈ R whenever (a, b) ∈ R, for all a, b ∈ A.
explanation: Symmetry means bidirectional relatedness: if a is related to b, then b is related to a.

question: Which three mathematical properties must a binary relation satisfy simultaneously to be classified as an equivalence relation?
options: Reflexive, Antisymmetric, and Transitive
Reflexive, Symmetric, and Transitive
Irreflexive, Symmetric, and Dense
Symmetric, Antisymmetric, and Asymmetric
evidence_quote: A relation on a set A is called an equivalence relation if it is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive.
explanation: An equivalence relation partitions a set into disjoint equivalence classes, which requires reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity.

question: In a Resource Allocation Graph where every resource has only a single instance, what does the presence of a cycle signify?
options: The system is guaranteed to be in a safe state with optimal throughput
The presence of a cycle is a necessary and sufficient condition confirming a deadlock
The cycle indicates memory fragmentation without causing deadlock
Single-instance resources cannot form cycles in a RAG
evidence_quote: If resources have single instance: In this case for Deadlock detection we can run an algorithm to check for cycle in RAG. Presence of cycle is the sufficient condition for deadlock.
explanation: For single-instance resource graphs, cycle detection is both necessary and sufficient to declare a deadlock.
